design:
Flow:
  type @ -> menu shows Specs and Files groups -> pick a spec -> a box [icon + title] replaces the typed @query
  or: side panel spec row / open spec header -> insert icon -> box at the composer's cursor
  send -> stored text carries kind, id, send-time title -> timeline renders the box with the current title -> click opens the spec in the side panel
  agent receives the same text and opens the document with read_spec_document

Decisions:
- D1. The reference is stored and delivered as text, so history, drafts, copying and every runner keep working. Recommended form: `[spec: <title at send time>](<document id>)`, for example `[spec: The spec header, redesigned](spdoc-407caf5abcdb)`. It names the kind, so an agent knows which tool opens it, and it does not begin with `@` (the Claude CLI expands `@x` into a file attachment, F409; hub/hub/file_mentions.py). The builder may choose a different form only if it meets the same requirements.
- D2. The id is the document id (`spdoc-...`), not the path: rename_spec_document changes the path, the id survives (the panel already keys spec tabs by id for this reason, hub/ui/src/store/panelTabsStore.ts).
- D3. The box displays the document's current title, resolved from the project's document list; the send-time title in the text is the fallback and the tooltip.
- D4. Files stay as they are in this slice: picking a file still inserts `@path` text. Making files boxes is slice `more-reference-kinds`.
- D5. A box is one unit in the composer. The composer is a plain textarea today, which cannot draw a box; replacing it is the main build cost of this slice, and it must keep the composer's existing behaviour (triggers, menu keys, drafts, growth, /model).
- D6. The browser drive for the UI tasks is one script, scripts/drive/d1112_spec_reference_box.py, extended by each UI task in order; the real agent turn is its own script, scripts/drive/d1112_spec_reference_agent_turn.py.

problem: To talk about a spec in a conversation, the operator copies its name or contents into the composer (operator, 2026-11-12: "Today I need to copy and paste the spec."). A copied title is ambiguous to the agent and goes stale on rename; copied contents bloat the prompt. The composer's `@` lists only files (hub/ui/src/lib/composerTriggerSources.ts), and what it inserts is loose text, not a unit the operator can see or delete as one. The operator asked that a reference "still be a string but boxed".

requirements.rationale: @ is the agreed trigger for references to things (operator, 2026-11-12); files must keep working while specs join them.
requirements.statement: When the operator opens an @ trigger in the composer, the menu SHALL list the project's specification documents under a Specs heading as well as the workspace files under a Files heading, each filtered by case-insensitive substring of the typed query (a spec matching on its title or its path), and SHALL keep the existing arrow, Enter, Tab and Escape behaviour across both groups.

Accepting a spec from the menu SHALL replace the typed @ and query with one reference shown as a box holding a spec icon and the document's title, followed by a space, with the cursor placed after it.

requirements.rationale: The operator asked for a reference that is boxed, not loose text that can be half-deleted into a broken string.
requirements.statement: In the composer a box SHALL behave as a single character: Backspace directly after it or Delete directly before it removes the whole box, the cursor cannot be placed inside it, and the left and right arrow keys move over it in one step.

requirements.rationale: A click already means open; one gesture with two meanings leaves the operator unsure which will happen.
requirements.statement: Each spec row in the side panel's spec list, and the header of a spec open in the side panel, SHALL offer an insert action distinct from opening it, which places a box for that spec at the composer's cursor (at the end when the composer has not been focused) and focuses the composer; clicking the spec itself SHALL still open it.

requirements.rationale: The operator did not know @ or $ existed (2026-11-12) although the placeholder names @.
requirements.statement: The composer SHALL show a visible control that opens the same reference menu at the cursor, and accepting a result from it SHALL insert exactly what typing @ would.

requirements.rationale: The id is unambiguous and survives renames; the agent reads the current version with its own tools; a leading @ makes the Claude CLI try to attach a file (F409).
requirements.statement: The message delivered to the agent SHALL contain, for each box, readable text naming the kind (spec), the document's id and its title at send time, and MUST NOT contain the document's contents for it; that text MUST NOT begin with @.

A composer draft containing boxes SHALL be restored with the same boxes after navigation or reload, and the stored message SHALL read as plain text wherever it is shown as text, such as when copied from the thread.

In the conversation timeline, the operator's sent message SHALL show each reference as the same box, displaying the document's current title, and activating the box SHALL open that document in the side panel.

requirements.rationale: An old message must not silently lose its subject.
requirements.statement: When the referenced document has been renamed since sending, its box SHALL show the current title and offer the title at send time as its tooltip; when the document no longer exists in the project's document list, the box SHALL show the title at send time in a muted style, marked as no longer available, and SHALL NOT open anything.

An agent that receives a message containing a spec box and no other naming of the document SHALL be able to open the referenced document by its id with the tools it already has, without instructions added for this purpose.

in_scope: Specification documents (change specs, roadmaps, capabilities) as the only boxed reference kind
The @ menu, the insert action in the side panel's spec list and an open spec's header, and a visible control that opens the menu without typing
How the box looks and behaves in the composer and in the operator's sent messages
non_goals: Boxes for files, tasks, requirements, agents or vault entries (slice more-reference-kinds)
Rendering ids that agents write in replies as boxes (slice references-in-replies)
Turning pasted links or ids into boxes (slice paste-becomes-reference)
Moving skills from $ to / and new / commands (slice slash-commands)
Inlining a spec's contents into the prompt
Dragging a spec into the composer

summary: Typing @ in the composer lists the project's specification documents beside files. Picking one, or pressing the insert action beside a spec in the side panel, puts a boxed reference into the message: one unit showing the spec's title. The sent message shows the same box, which opens the spec, and the agent receives the spec's kind, id and title as plain text it can act on.
